summary: Join our M&E training course to master survey design and execution. Gain essential skills for effective monitoring and evaluation in various fields.
lede: Designing and conducting surveys for monitoring and evaluation is a structured workflow for connecting evaluation questions to a Theory of Change, logframe, OECD DAC evaluation criteria, measurable indicators, and programme decisions. The course develops practical skills in sampling, unbiased question design, enumerator training, fieldwork quality, digital data capture, and interpretation against programme targets. You will build an indicator-to-question matrix, calculate a basic sample size, draft a questionnaire, configure a KoboToolbox or ODK form, apply skip logic, review missing-data patterns, and prepare a descriptive analysis plan. The workflow also covers informed consent, confidentiality, data minimization, transparent trade-offs, and presenting findings through a dashboard or decision brief.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who translate programme objectives into survey evidence, manage field data collection, or use evaluation findings to guide decisions. It suits foundation-to-intermediate learners who need a complete and practical M&E survey design process.
audience: Learning and Adaptation Leads using survey findings
prerequisites: You need basic experience with programme activities, monitoring indicators, or operational reporting. You do not need prior survey software or statistical programming experience. A laptop with a modern web browser is recommended for the KoboToolbox or ODK configuration exercise. Advanced weighting, psychometric validation, causal inference, and complex statistical modelling are introduced conceptually rather than taught as technical implementation.
topics: Data collection, survey design & mobile tools
